title: A clustered data-centre shutdown shows why AI loads need grid-aware failover
friendlyTitle: AI data centres need smarter backup-power switching
summary: After a power-line failure near Washington, roughly 3.1 gigawatts of data-centre load disconnected from the PJM grid within about 30 seconds, contributing to a voltage spike and an extended recovery. Engineers say staggered switching and campus-scale energy storage could make these large loads less disruptive.
friendlySummary: A power-line problem caused many data centres to leave the grid almost together. That sudden change made the electricity system harder to stabilise.
whyItMatters: AI infrastructure affects the reliability and cost of the same electricity system used by homes and other businesses. Data-centre operators and policymakers need to evaluate coordinated failover behaviour, not only total energy consumption.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Large AI facilities share the grid with homes and businesses. Better timing and battery systems can reduce flickering, outages and wider grid problems.
